calls.reason: The packet shows no clear downturn among startups building on these models. SimpleClosure's H1 2026 data shows AI's share of shutdowns falling, and the Builder.ai insolvency is one isolated failure. The condition the forecast depends on has not been shown to occur.

The HandRefiner paper (Nov 2023) says diffusion models still botch hands because learning hand structure is hard. OpenAI's Sora page lists object errors, and a CVPR 2024 paper calls hand artifacts common. Midjourney v5's improvement shows progress but not reliable hands.

The Guardian reported that Microsoft replaced MSN's human curators with automation in 2020. CNN's sources tied MSN's false stories to that switch. Futurism and Windows Central documented Bigfoot stories and a garbled, plagiarized obituary. 'Destroyed' is hyperbole, but the substance holds.

This is an undated, hedged ('I believe') forecast. The October 2026 sell-off reports mix AI financing worries with oil prices and competition, and show no severe industry-wide damage caused by a collapse in AI expectations.

The only evidence is Synergy's figure that three firms held 67% of cloud infrastructure in Q4 2023. That measures a different market and does not trace what share of AI-product spending reaches those firms, so 'almost every dollar' cannot be judged.

OpenAI said Azure is the exclusive cloud for all of its workloads, including inference, and Google said Claude runs on Google Cloud. With his 'on some level' hedge, serving each interaction plausibly produces big-tech revenue, though the billing and credit terms are not public.
